comparison: Both address absolute suppression claims (C34, C35, C50, C100). OpenEval finds these claims SUPPORTED, noting they strengthen the interpretation of BOLD deactivation reflecting neural suppression, though acknowledging potential statistical power limitations. Peer reviewers rate this UNCERTAIN, stating the data are 'insufficiently supported' and not shown separately, and questioning whether the experimental design can distinguish lower firing rates from genuine suppression without a true baseline.

Both evaluate temporal characterization claims (C32, C33). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with appropriate statistical tests, though noting bootstrap method details could be more explicit. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED without challenge, accepting these as supporting data for main results.

Both address the central finding of BOLD-neural correspondence (C30, C31, C98, C99). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, calling this a 'key novel contribution' with strong effect sizes. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, expressing concern that positive BOLD/activation was shown in one patient while negative BOLD/suppression was in the other patient, and questioning the lack of true baseline in the SSVEP paradigm.

OpenEval R10 synthesizes main findings (C36-C41) including claims C39, C40, C41 which overlap with peer R1. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED despite n=2 limitation. Peer R1 addresses overlapping claims C39, C40, C41 (plus C98, C99, C30, C31) but rates UNCERTAIN due to design concerns about showing both effects in both patients.

Both evaluate fMRI localization findings (C18, C19, C102-C105). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, noting consistency with prior literature though acknowledging spatial uncertainty from electrode localization. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, accepting the anatomical correspondence as demonstrated without challenge.

Both address face-selectivity findings. OpenEval R6 covers C27-C29, C97 and rates SUPPORTED but questions the extraordinarily high percentages (>85%) and potential selection bias. Peer R3 covers C16, C17, C27, C28, C97 and rates SUPPORTED, describing methods as 'robust and well-established' and the dataset as 'valuable' without expressing concerns about the high percentages.

Both address hemispheric differences and broader literature context (C43, C44). OpenEval R12 also includes C45 and rates SUPPORTED, noting consistency strengthens findings despite small sample. Peer R8 rates SUPPORTED, accepting this as established knowledge used to justify study design.

Both address spike sorting and recording methods. OpenEval R5 covers C22-C26, C76-C84 and rates SUPPORTED with standard practices, though noting brief recording time and unaddressed stability concerns. Peer R6 covers C24, C25, C26, C45 and rates SUPPORTED, acknowledging the dataset as 'valuable' with 'many recording sessions and neurons' without challenging quantitative findings.

Both address participant and methodological setup. OpenEval R2 covers extensive methods (C9-C21, C54-C65) and rates SUPPORTED with clear descriptions, though noting temporal gap concerns. Peer R7 covers subset (C9, C12, C14, C20, C21, C54) and rates SUPPORTED, describing it as 'ingenious use of clinical patient data' and noting value of recordings.

Both address experimental paradigm. OpenEval R3 covers C16, C17, C66-C75, C101 and rates SUPPORTED, noting well-validated paradigm but questioning frequency differences between fMRI and electrophysiology. Peer R3 covers C16, C17, C27, C28, C97 and rates SUPPORTED, accepting methods as 'robust and well-established.'

OpenEval R1 evaluates prior knowledge and background claims (C1-C8), rating them SUPPORTED as accurately summarizing the state of knowledge with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background/introduction claims.

OpenEval R11 addresses mechanistic speculation about spike suppression sources (C42), rating it UNCERTAIN as plausible but not directly supported by presented evidence. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this speculative claim.

OpenEval R13 evaluates comparative neuroscience context (C46-C51), rating SUPPORTED with appropriate citations to monkey studies and limitations of animal models. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these comparative/contextual claims.

OpenEval R14 addresses prior work on inhibitory function (C52, C53), rating SUPPORTED as relevant background knowledge with appropriate references. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background citations.

OpenEval R15 evaluates comprehensive fMRI methods (C85-C96), rating SUPPORTED with standard acquisition parameters and well-established analysis approaches, though noting 6-8 week gap concerns. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these detailed fMRI methodology claims.

OpenEval R16 addresses specific analysis details for isolating face-selective responses (C106, C107), rating SUPPORTED with appropriate notch-filtering approach. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific analysis methodology claims.
